properties.statement:
MEASURED ON THE v0.30.0 CUT, 2026-08-13, and it produced a WRONG COMMITTED RECORD that every other check passed.

THREE BINARY VERSIONS WERE IN PLAY ON ONE MACHINE:

    live MCP server    0.29.0 image   (the session's own tools)
    target/release/    0.28.0, Aug 11 (**what `tools/reflow2_cli.py`'s DEFAULT_BIN resolves to**)
    target/debug/      0.30.0         (built minutes earlier, the only correct one)

The release procedure's replay exists precisely to avoid the live server's old stamp: import into a temp store, export from it with the NEW binary. I ran that replay and passed `C.DEFAULT_BIN`. **The committed export came back stamped `0.28.0` — with PERFECTLY CORRECT LINEAGE**, `prev_content_hash` equal to main's `content_hash`, 2144 nodes, 8447 edges, `graph_id: reflow2`. Every property anyone checks was right except the one that says which reflow2 wrote it. Caught only by reading `stamp.reflow2_version` out of the written file before committing.

⭐⭐ AND THE EXISTING STALENESS CAPABILITY CANNOT SEE THIS, WHICH IS THE FINDING. `cap:the-server-knows-its-own-currency` reports whether **the server's own executable has been REPLACED SINCE IT STARTED** — `ver:the-server-says-when-it-is-stale` demonstrates it by relinking a binary under a running daemon and watching the same server flip to `stale: true`. A server freshly spawned from a THREE-VERSION-OLD build has had nothing replaced under it, so it reads a definite **`stale: false`** and is telling the truth.

⇒ **"MY EXECUTABLE CHANGED UNDER ME" AND "I AM AN OLD BUILD" ARE DIFFERENT FACTS, AND ONLY THE FIRST IS DETECTED.** The second is the one that mis-stamps a release record, and it is undetectable from inside the server: the binary is internally consistent and confident. It is visible only by comparing the stamp against the version the SOURCE claims.

📌 THE NARROW FIX IS FREE AND IS NOW IN [[reflow2-release-cut-procedure]]: name the freshly built binary explicitly in the replay, never `DEFAULT_BIN`, and READ `stamp.reflow2_version` OUT OF THE WRITTEN FILE BEFORE COMMITTING — every cut, every time.

📌 THE WIDER ONE IS NOT TAKEN AND IS NOT OBVIOUS: whether `reflow2_cli.py` should refuse, or at least say, when the binary it is about to drive reports a version older than the workspace's `Cargo.toml`. That is a comparison the CLI can make and currently does not, and it is the same shape as every other finding in this increment — the information existed and did not reach the person.

⚠️ STILL TRUE AT SESSION END: `target/release/reflow2-mcp` on this machine remains **0.28.0**. CI builds its own release artifacts, so the PUBLISHED v0.30.0 binaries are unaffected; anything local defaulting to that path is driving a three-version-old server.
